speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office, please take a seat. I am Dr. Agent, and I need to understand your skin concerns; can you describe the specific lesion(s) you are worried about, including when they first appeared and how they have changed?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history; the failure of prior treatments for syphilis and eczema alongside your heavy smoking history is concerning. To better evaluate these non-healing, crusty lesions on your penis and finger, can you describe their exact appearance, size, and if you have noticed any bleeding, pain, or discharge?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC). The presentation of non-healing, painless, crusty lesions on sun-exposed skin (finger) and a high-risk mucosal site (penis) in a heavy smoker with failed prior treatments is highly suggestive of SCC.
